findings.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with a '80%' percentage string where the (new) signature expects a WxH dimensions string, and with tempfile.path as both input and output. ImageMagick convert invoked by convert_with reads and writes the same path; on several ImageMagick versions convert refuses or truncates the in-place output, leaving a zero-byte/corrupt tempfile that then goes to Upload.create_for, producing a broken or failed upload.

[BUG] resize and downsize signatures change from (from, to, width, height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), but existing call sites in the codebase pass width and height as separate positional args. At existing call sites (e.g. avatar/thumbnail resizing elsewhere in the repo calling OptimizedImage.resize(path, path, w, h)), the height integer lands in the opts parameter slot, dimensions becomes just the width (yielding instructions like '-resize 100x' with no height and opts[:allow_animation] evaluated on an Integer), producing malformed convert commands and broken thumbnails instead of resized images.

[BUG] The animated-GIF branch in optimize matches from =~ /\.GIF$/i, but tempfile.path is an extension-less temp filename, so the animated instruction path can never trigger for the new downsize loop. Animated GIFs uploaded through this path are downsized with the static instructions, which drops animation frames (convert on a single frame), so animated uploads become static images silently.

[BUG] The loop performs at most 5 downsizes of ~80% each, which only shrinks a file by a factor of ~3.1, while max_image_size_kb can be far below the hard-coded 10MB client cap. A 9MB image with max_image_size_kb=4096 exits the loop still above the limit and proceeds to Upload.create_for, so the advertised 'automatically reduced to allowed size' behavior fails and the user still gets a file-too-large error (or an oversized upload is stored) for any image larger than ~3x the configured max.

[ADVISORY] The client-side hard-coded 10MB cap no longer matches any server-side SiteSetting, while the controller still uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb for the same decision. Operators who lower max_image_size_kb get client-side rejections at 10MB for files the server would accept and downsize, and files between the server limit and 10MB hit the expensive server-side ImageMagick loop on every upload; the two limits will silently drift.

[BUG] resize/downsize arity changed from (from, to, width, height) to (from, to, dimensions) but the diff does not update any existing call sites, so every in-tree caller of OptimizedImage.resize(path, path, w, h) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Every code path that generates optimized thumbnails (avatar resizing, post image thumbnails, crawler views) crashes at runtime after this diff, because the method now takes 3 positional args plus opts instead of 4.

[BUG] The dimensions(width, height) helper is deleted while the signature of optimize changes, so any remaining callers of OptimizedImage.dimensions also break with NoMethodError. Code outside this diff that built dimension strings via the removed helper fails with NoMethodError.

[BUG] The downsize loop never verifies success: if OptimizedImage.downsize fails (convert_with returns false, e.g. ImageMagick missing or a corrupted image), the loop keeps decrementing attempts and proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized (or partially overwritten/corrupted) tempfile, silently bypassing SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb entirely. A user can end up with an uploaded file larger than the configured max_image_size_kb, or a corrupted image stored as the upload, with no error raised and no feedback; the previous hard enforcement of the size limit on the server is lost.

[BUG] The API/URL download path (FileHelper.download limit raised from max_image_size_kb to 10MB) combined with the loop capped at 5 attempts means a large remote image (e.g. 50MB via API URL) that cannot be reduced below max_image_size_kb in 5 passes is still uploaded at full size above the site limit. max_image_size_kb is no longer an enforced limit for API URL uploads; an oversized upload is stored silently, defeating the setting the feature is supposed to preserve.

[BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes 10MB instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so files between max_image_size_kb and 10MB now pass client validation (intended), but files the site admin set above 10MB, or below, produce contradictory behavior and the alert text 'file_too_large { max_size_kb: 10240 }' lies about the actual limit. Admins who configured max_*_size_kb see the wrong limit in the error message, and the three hardcoded 10MB values (client check, 413 handler, server download cap) can drift independently; there is no single source of truth.

[ADVISORY] The same 10MB constant is duplicated in three places (utilities.js line 182, utilities.js line 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55) with no shared constant, a parallel hand-maintained enumeration. The next change to the upload size cap requires updating three independent sites; missing one yields client/server inconsistency that only surfaces in production.

[BUG] No acceptance criterion or edge case in the diff handles non-image files that pass FileHelper.is_image? but cannot be downsized (e.g. SVG, animated WebP): the loop calls ImageMagick downsize on them and, on failure or partial write, uploads the result without checking the output is still a valid image. A corrupted or zero-byte tempfile can be committed as an Upload after a failed downsize pass, since tempfile.size is re-read but its integrity never verified.

[ADVISORY] The feature depends on the web server (nginx client_max_body_size) accepting bodies up to 10MB, but the diff ships no configuration change or documentation of that requirement, so in default installs nginx rejects anything above its configured limit with 413 before Rails ever sees the file and the whole feature is inert. Users uploading images between nginx's body limit and 10MB get the generic 413 bootbox (whose hardcoded 10MB message is also wrong for their actual server limit), and admins cannot know the downsize feature requires raising client_max_body_size.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff covers any of the new behavior: the downsize loop (attempt count, failure handling, size re-check), the API URL download cap change, or the optimized_image signature change; the only touched spec-shaped surface is absent entirely. A regression in the loop (e.g. infinite overwrite of the tempfile or failure to shrink) would ship unnoticed, and the signature change to OptimizedImage.resize/downsize breaks call sites no test guards.

[BUG] The diff replaces the per-type SiteSettings lookup (`max_' + type + '_size_kb`) with a hardcoded 10MB client-side limit, work that is not traceable to the stated downsize feature and silently changes upload validation behavior. Admin-configured size limits are no longer enforced in the client: a site with max_attachment_size_kb of 2MB now accepts files up to 10MB in the browser, and the bootbox error message reports '10240' instead of the configured limit.

[BUG] The 413 handler now hardcodes `10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, unrelated to the downsize feature. When the server rejects an oversized upload with 413 (i.e. the file exceeded max_image_size_kb and was not downsized, e.g. non-image or the downsize path failed), the user is shown an error claiming the limit is 10MB regardless of the actual configured setting, so the error is wrong for any site not configured at 10MB.

[BUG] The downsize loop does not enforce the stated invariant: it gives up after 5 attempts or on OptimizedImage failure (convert_with returns false and is ignored) and still proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversized tempfile. A >max_image_size_kb image for which ImageMagick fails (or that 5 rounds of 80% downsizing cannot reduce) is stored anyway, so the 'automatically reduced to allowed size' guarantee the feature commits to does not hold and oversized uploads reach post rendering.

[ADVISORY] The magic constant `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0` re-purposes the setting as an on/off feature flag with no documented meaning or admin UI change in this diff. Operators setting max_image_size_kb to 0 (previously plausibly 'unlimited') now silently disable automatic downsizing and get hard upload failures instead; there is no writer/path in this diff that communicates this new semantics.

[ADVISORY] Three independent hardcoded occurrences of the 10MB value (utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, uploads_controller.rb:53) replace what were three reads of settings, creating a hand-maintained parallel enumeration of one constant. The next change to the transfer limit must be applied in three places across two languages; missing one produces client/server limit mismatch that surfaces only as confusing 413 errors.

[ADVISORY] The public `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature changes from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts) as incidental refactoring inside a feature PR, while out-of-tree/plugin callers of the old arity are silently affected. Any plugin calling the old 5-argument downsize gets its max_width string interpolated as dimensions, producing garbage ImageMagick instructions instead of an error; the API break is not mentioned as part of the feature.

[BUG] The public OptimizedImage.downsize signature was changed from downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts), breaking every existing call site that still passes (width, height) or (width, height, opts) — the old third argument (an integer width) is now interpreted as the dimensions string and the fourth lands in opts, so those callers pass an Integer where a String is interpolated into an ImageMagick command or raise on opts[:allow_animation] being an Integer. All pre-existing downsize/resize callers outside this diff (upload pipeline, cookers) silently misroute or crash at runtime; only the single new call in uploads_controller.rb matches the new signature.

[BUG] The client-side size check now hardcodes 10*1024 KB instead of reading Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], while the server still enforces SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb / per-type settings — a parallel source of truth that diverges the moment an admin changes the setting. With max_image_size_kb set below 10MB, a file under 10MB passes the client check but the downsize loop cannot shrink it and the upload fails with a confusing error; with the setting above 10MB, small legitimate uploads are rejected client-side that the server would accept. Same divergence at line 243 for the 413 handler, which reports the hardcoded 10MB regardless of the actual configured limit.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions inline in the upload request path with no cap on the input size (API/programmatic uploads never pass through the client-side check). A large upload (e.g. 100MB) triggers 5 sequential convert processes on one request thread — multi-second-to-minute request latency and an easy resource-exhaustion vector via authenticated uploads.

[ADVISORY] Five 80% downsizes reduce pixel area to ~0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original, so files above roughly 3x the limit (or formats that compress poorly) still exceed max_image_size_kb after the loop exits and fail upstream with the generic 'file too large' error. Users uploading large-but-legal-under-the-new-flow images get an unexplained rejection after the server already did the expensive shrink work.

[ADVISORY] The literal 10 * 1024 is duplicated in three places across two languages (utilities.js lines 182 and 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55), with the unit expressed only in adjacent comments. The next editor who changes one copy (or typos 84600-style) gets silent divergence between client validation, 413 error text, and server enforcement — exactly the drift the per-type SiteSetting previously prevented.

[BUG] The client-side file-size check is changed from the site-configurable SiteSettings limit to a hardcoded 10MB, silently removing the admin-configurable max_{type}_size_kb enforcement the original upload feature promised. Sites with max_attachment_size_kb below 10MB now accept client-side files up to 10MB that get rejected only after upload; sites configured above 10MB now wrongly reject valid files at the client with a message citing a limit the admin never set. This objective change (ignoring site settings) is unrelated to the PR's stated intent of downsizing images and was never explicitly accepted.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message lies about the actual configured limit. A user whose upload is rejected by the server with 413 is told the max size is 10MB even when the server's real limit is, say, 4MB or 40MB, directing them to resize to the wrong dimension and producing confusing support reports.

[BUG] The public OptimizedImage.downsize signature is changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), breaking every existing out-of-diff call site that passes four positional arguments. Existing callers passing (path, path, 1024, 768, opts) now bind 768 to opts and pass a Hash where a dimensions string is expected ("#{max_width}x#{max_height}" becomes e.g. "1024x768" only by accident of interpolation, while opts['allow_animation'] lookups hit the integer), producing wrong or crashing image processing in thumbnail generation paths outside this diff. Renaming an internal helper used only here would have been safe; changing the shared public method silently changed the objective for all callers.

[BUG] The downsize loop can still leave tempfile.size above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts (attempt counter decrements even on failed downsizes), so an oversized upload is created anyway. A user uploads a huge or incompressible image; after 5 downsize passes (or 5 failed convert runs) the file still exceeds the limit but Upload.create_for proceeds, storing an upload larger than the site's configured maximum — the exact constraint the setting is meant to enforce.

[ADVISORY] The animated-GIF branch in OptimizedImage depends on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the tempfile passed here is a Tempfile whose random path has no .gif extension, so downsize_instructions_animated is never selected for downloaded/uploaded GIFs. Animated GIFs larger than the limit get resized with the non-animated instructions path, which can strip animation or misprocess the frames; whoever relies on animated thumbnails for downsized GIFs gets silently broken behavior.

[ADVISORY] Downsizing runs unconditionally on every large image upload with no setting to disable it, changing accepted upload semantics (content is now silently modified server-side) without a feature flag. Admins whose intent was to enforce a hard size cap (reject, not mutate) now get lossy in-place rewriting of user content with quality "80%" applied up to 5 times (cascading re-compression), and cannot turn the behavior off without a code change; the original file bytes are destroyed since downsize writes to tempfile.path in place.

[BUG] The automatic downsize path runs ImageMagick (via OptimizedImage.downsize → convert_with's backtick shell invocation) on any file whose name passes FileHelper.is_image?, so a user-supplied SVG (or other delegate-handled format) is processed by ImageMagick during upload. If FileHelper.is_image? admits SVG by extension, an attacker uploading a crafted SVG triggers ImageMagick delegate processing (ImageTragick-class delegate/command-injection surface) on the server; the new call site expands the set of user-controlled bytes fed to convert.

[BUG] The server-side download limit is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, ignoring SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb that previously bounded the API URL fetch. An admin who configures max_image_size_kb to a small value (e.g. 1024 KB) still has the server fetch up to 10 MB from arbitrary API-supplied URLs, removing the configured resource bound and increasing the fetch/memory footprint per request; the client-side hardcode at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 likewise overrides the admin's setting, so users can push 10 MB files regardless of configured policy.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop performs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions per upload inside the request cycle whenever tempfile.size exceeds the configured limit, with no check that each iteration actually shrinks the file. Any authenticated user can upload a large (up to 10 MB, per the new hardcoded ceiling) image and force five sequential ImageMagick invocations per request; concurrent uploads become a cheap CPU-exhaustion DoS vector, and a pathological file that doesn't shrink under '80%' burns all 5 attempts every time.

[ADVISORY] convert_with builds a shell command by string-interpolating the instruction array (which embeds the from/to file paths) directly into backticks with no escaping. Any current or future caller that passes a path derived from user input (e.g. a filename containing shell metacharacters) into resize/downsize achieves arbitrary command execution; the diff routes tempfile paths through this sink today (safe), but the new public downsize(from, to, dimensions) signature makes it easier for later call sites to feed attacker-influenced strings into the unescaped interpolation.

[ADVISORY] Client-side size enforcement is now a hardcoded 10 MB constant instead of the site setting, diverging from the server's configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The client-side check and the server-side check now use different sources of truth: an admin lowering max_image_size_kb sees the server still accept (then downsized) 10 MB client-accepted uploads, and the 413 handler at line 246 reports a hardcoded '10 MB' that no longer matches what the server actually enforces, confusing users about why uploads fail.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize's arity was changed from 4 parameters (from, to, max_width, max_height) to 3 (from, to, dimensions), so any existing caller invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) now passes the height integer into the opts position. Such callers produce dimensions string "#{width}x" and then crash on opts[:allow_animation] (NoMethodError on Integer), or silently generate a malformed ImageMagick instruction, breaking thumbnail/avatar generation that previously worked.

[BUG] The downsize loop re-checks tempfile.size but never verifies after the 5 attempts that the file actually dropped below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, so the upload proceeds oversized when 0.8^5 (≈33%) reduction is insufficient. A file larger than ~3x the configured limit (e.g. 35MB with a 10MB setting) exhausts 5 iterations, remains over the limit, and is still created via Upload.create_for — the very oversized upload this feature was meant to prevent, which then fails downstream or bloats storage.

[BUG] The client-side max size check was changed from the SiteSettings value max_' + type + '_size_kb to a hardcoded 10MB, decoupling the browser-side validation from the server's configured limits. Sites with a smaller configured file/image limit no longer get a friendly client-side bootbox warning and instead hit the server-side rejection path (or the auto-downsize path), and the 413 handler now reports 'max_size_kb: 10240' even when the actual server limit differs, showing users a wrong number.

[BUG] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb, so the message shown to users contradicts the actual server configuration whenever the admin sets a different value. Users uploading images to a site configured with, say, a 4MB limit see 'file too large, max is 10240 KB' after the server rejects a 5MB upload — misleading error message with no path to configure it.

[ADVISORY] The new auto-downsize branch (attempt loop, is_image? gate, in-place tempfile rewrite) is behavioral logic with no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in the loop condition, the is_image? guard, or OptimizedImage.downsize's new '80%' percentage-dimensions contract would silently corrupt or reject image uploads without any spec failing.

[ADVISORY] The dimensions() helper was deleted and optimize()'s signature changed from (width, height, opts) to (dimensions, opts), a silent public-API change to a model method other in-tree and plugin code calls. Out-of-tree callers of OptimizedImage.optimize/resize with the old 5-arg form pass an opts hash into the dimensions interpolation ('#{width}x#{height}' producing garbage like '[object Object]x') — silently malformed convert instructions rather than a loud argument error.

[BUG] The downsizing loop overwrites the user's original uploaded tempfile in place (downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)) before Upload.create_for, permanently destroying the original image bytes with no backup or rollback path. A user uploading a 9MB PNG against max_image_size_kb=1024 receives a ~0.8^5≈33%-scale image (compounded five re-resample passes, visibly degraded quality) and the original is unrecoverable — silent data loss on the only copy of the file; if convert fails (exit status ignored by convert_with), the oversized file is uploaded anyway and fails with 413 upstream.

[BUG] The public OptimizedImage.resize/downsize signatures changed from (from, to, width, height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), so all existing in-tree callers still passing width and height as separate args now pass height into the opts slot. Callers like create_optimized_image invoke downsize(from, to, w, h, opts): w becomes the dimensions string, h lands in opts, and opts[:allow_animation] raises NoMethodError on an Integer (or silently skips the animated branch), so every optimized-image generation path that calls the old 4-arg form breaks at runtime after this diff deploys.

[BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes 10MB and the 413 handler hardcodes the same value, discarding the SiteSettings-driven limits (max_image_size_kb and max_<type>_size_kb) that admins configure. Admins who set max_*_size_kb below 10MB can no longer enforce it client-side — oversized files are uploaded, then either silently downsized server-side or rejected with a misleading 'max_size_kb: 10240' message that contradicts the configured setting; config is silently ignored with no migration of the setting value.

[BUG] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit and writes its output to /dev/null), so a failed ImageMagick conversion leaves the original oversized tempfile in place and the upload proceeds. When ImageMagick is missing, fails on a corrupt/animated image, or repeatedly cannot shrink below the limit, the controller silently uploads a file larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and returns success — the API reports success while dropping the size-enforcement work the feature exists to provide.

[BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes 10*1024 KB instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the alert can display a limit that is not the site's actual configured limit. On a site with max_image_size_kb set below 10MB, users uploading a 9MB image see no client-side error (correct, it will be downsized), but on any file type routed through this shared validator the user is told the limit is 10240 KB while the server enforces a different configured value — the error content misdirects debugging and misrepresents the enforced limit.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10 MB in the user-facing message even though the server that returned 413 enforced the web server's own configured body limit, which may be smaller or larger. A user whose 20MB upload is rejected by nginx with 413 is told the max size is 10240 KB; if the reverse proxy limit is 5MB the message is wrong, and if the admin set a larger limit the message understates what is allowed — misleading error content on a user-facing path.

[ADVISORY] The loop attempts 5 downsizes with no break on conversion failure and no logging, so 5 identical failing ImageMagick invocations run per oversized upload with no observability of why the file was still oversized. On a site with a broken ImageMagick install, every large-image upload pays 5 wasted subprocess spawns (a per-request amplification on the upload path) and operators get no signal that downsizing never worked — the feature is silently inert until a user complains.

[ADVISORY] The public OptimizedImage.downsize signature changes from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions-string) while keeping the same method name, so any existing caller still passing two numeric arguments silently produces the malformed geometry string "80x50%"-style input instead of failing loudly at a renamed method. In-tree or plugin callers of downsize that were not updated pass (w, h) and get a single "WxH"-interpreted string built from "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" only if they happen to pass two args — a caller passing two numbers now hits ArgumentError on the 3-arg arity, but a caller adapted to pass one string in the old percent format is indistinguishable from a caller passing a broken dimension; a rename to downsize_by_dimensions would have made stale callers fail loudly instead of producing corrupt convert instructions.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing feature is gated directly on the raw SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb value with no dedicated setting, so admins who want to keep a strict upload limit have no way to disable auto-downsizing, and the client hardcode means the effective behavior cannot be turned off without a code deploy. An admin whose compliance policy requires rejecting oversized files outright gets them silently shrunk and accepted instead; there is no feature flag or setting to restore the previous reject behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e., the same path is used for both input and output, and `convert_with` shells out to ImageMagick without any guard against in-place writes. The assertion that this will definitely truncate/produce zero-byte files depends on external ImageMagick behavior not shown in the diff.

From this diff alone, `downsize`’s effective signature becomes `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`, so any existing callers still passing `(from, to, width, height, opts)` would mis-bind arguments and likely error when `optimize` does `opts[:allow_animation]`. However, the finding overstates that `resize` also changed signature—`resize` still takes `(from, to, width, height, opts={})` in the diff. Also, the existence of such call sites elsewhere can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload downsize loop, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes `from` as `tempfile.path`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop performs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions per upload inside the request cycle whenever tempfile.size exceeds the configured limit, with no check that each iteration actually shrinks the file. Any authenticated user can upload a large (up to 10 MB, per the new hardcoded ceiling) image and force five sequential ImageMagick invocations per request; concurrent uploads become a cheap CPU-exhaustion DoS vector, and a pathological file that doesn't shrink under '80%' burns all 5 attempts every time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 ImageMagick conversions per request: `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes; OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. There is no check that a given iteration actually reduces the file size; if `tempfile.size` remains above the limit (e.g., a file that doesn’t shrink under the chosen parameters), it will burn all 5 attempts every time. Since `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately shells out (`convert_with` uses backticks), concurrent uploads can force repeated expensive CPU work inside the request cycle, creating a practical DoS vector. The change also hardcodes a 10MB ceiling in JS and API download, aligning with the finding’s stated bound.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] convert_with builds a shell command by string-interpolating the instruction array (which embeds the from/to file paths) directly into backticks with no escaping. Any current or future caller that passes a path derived from user input (e.g. a filename containing shell metacharacters) into resize/downsize achieves arbitrary command execution; the diff routes tempfile paths through this sink today (safe), but the new public downsize(from, to, dimensions) signature makes it easier for later call sites to feed attacker-influenced strings into the unescaped interpolation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedImage.convert_with` still executes a shell command via backticks using `instructions.join(" ")` with no escaping in this method, and the refactor changes the API (adds/overrides `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) and introduces a new caller from `uploads_controller.rb`. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that any caller can pass user-influenced paths into `from`/`to` (the new caller uses `tempfile.path`), nor can we see whether `*_instructions` already shell-escapes paths. So the “arbitrary command execution” claim isn’t directly provable from this diff, but the unescaped shell execution remains a real, diff-touched design risk worth noting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Client-side size enforcement is now a hardcoded 10 MB constant instead of the site setting, diverging from the server's configurable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The client-side check and the server-side check now use different sources of truth: an admin lowering max_image_size_kb sees the server still accept (then downsized) 10 MB client-accepted uploads, and the 413 handler at line 246 reports a hardcoded '10 MB' that no longer matches what the server actually enforces, confusing users about why uploads fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the max upload size checks are changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in both the pre-upload check and the 413 handler. Meanwhile, the server still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for the new downsizing loop and previously used it for URL download size limits (now also hardcoded to 10MB). This creates an inconsistent/misleading client-side limit and error messaging that can diverge from admin-configured server limits, leading to confusing failures or behavior differences.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize's arity was changed from 4 parameters (from, to, max_width, max_height) to 3 (from, to, dimensions), so any existing caller invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) now passes the height integer into the opts position. Such callers produce dimensions string "#{width}x" and then crash on opts[:allow_animation] (NoMethodError on Integer), or silently generate a malformed ImageMagick instruction, breaking thumbnail/avatar generation that previously worked.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` is first changed to accept `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, but then the diff *redefines* `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` later, which overrides the earlier definition. As a result, existing callers using `downsize(from, to, width, height)` will bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (an Integer). `optimize` then does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on Integer, and/or pass a non-string `dimensions` into instruction generation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop re-checks tempfile.size but never verifies after the 5 attempts that the file actually dropped below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, so the upload proceeds oversized when 0.8^5 (≈33%) reduction is insufficient. A file larger than ~3x the configured limit (e.g. 35MB with a 10MB setting) exhausts 5 iterations, remains over the limit, and is still created via Upload.create_for — the very oversized upload this feature was meant to prevent, which then fails downstream or bloats storage.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop downsizes at most 5 times while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but after the loop it unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` with no check that the file is now within the limit. From the diff alone, an image that remains oversized after 5 iterations would still be uploaded, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side max size check was changed from the SiteSettings value max_' + type + '_size_kb to a hardcoded 10MB, decoupling the browser-side validation from the server's configured limits. Sites with a smaller configured file/image limit no longer get a friendly client-side bootbox warning and instead hit the server-side rejection path (or the auto-downsize path), and the 413 handler now reports 'max_size_kb: 10240' even when the actual server limit differs, showing users a wrong number.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the client-side max size checks from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in `utilities.js`. This decouples browser validation and the displayed `max_size_kb` error message from the server/site configuration, so sites with smaller configured limits will not get the correct client-side warning and the 413 handler will report 10240KB regardless of actual settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb, so the message shown to users contradicts the actual server configuration whenever the admin sets a different value. Users uploading images to a site configured with, say, a 4MB limit see 'file too large, max is 10240 KB' after the server rejects a 5MB upload — misleading error message with no path to configure it.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 handler and the earlier file-size check both changed from using `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_*_size_kb` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the user-facing `file_too_large` message will always claim 10240 KB regardless of the configured site setting, so it can mislead users on sites with different admin-configured limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new auto-downsize branch (attempt loop, is_image? gate, in-place tempfile rewrite) is behavioral logic with no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in the loop condition, the is_image? guard, or OptimizedImage.downsize's new '80%' percentage-dimensions contract would silently corrupt or reject image uploads without any spec failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `uploads_controller.rb` (a 5-iteration loop that conditionally rewrites the uploaded tempfile in-place via `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and size exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`). The diff also changes `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` to accept a single `dimensions` argument (and `resize/downsize` now pass strings like "#{w}x#{h}"). No test/spec changes are included in this diff, so regressions in the guard/loop or the new "80%" contract would not be caught by tests shown here. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dimensions() helper was deleted and optimize()'s signature changed from (width, height, opts) to (dimensions, opts), a silent public-API change to a model method other in-tree and plugin code calls. Out-of-tree callers of OptimizedImage.optimize/resize with the old 5-arg form pass an opts hash into the dimensions interpolation ('#{width}x#{height}' producing garbage like '[object Object]x') — silently malformed convert instructions rather than a loud argument error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `OptimizedImage.optimize`’s method signature from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={})` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, and it also redefines `downsize` to take a single `dimensions` argument (the later `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overrides the earlier 4-arg version). That is a real compatibility/API surface change that could break out-of-tree/plugin callers relying on the old arity. However, the finding’s claim that this would “silently” produce malformed dimension strings is not supported by the new Ruby signatures (old-arity calls would typically raise `ArgumentError` due to wrong number of arguments, not quietly interpolate “[object Object]x”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsizing loop overwrites the user's original uploaded tempfile in place (downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)) before Upload.create_for, permanently destroying the original image bytes with no backup or rollback path. A user uploading a 9MB PNG against max_image_size_kb=1024 receives a ~0.8^5≈33%-scale image (compounded five re-resample passes, visibly degraded quality) and the original is unrecoverable — silent data loss on the only copy of the file; if convert fails (exit status ignored by convert_with), the oversized file is uploaded anyway and fails with 413 upstream.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an in-place mutation of the uploaded tempfile before `Upload.create_for` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` inside a loop). That means the server will no longer persist the originally uploaded bytes for oversized images; it will persist a repeatedly recompressed version, and it may take up to 5 successive downsizes (quality degradation risk). Also, `OptimizedImage.convert_with` can return `false` on failure, but the controller ignores the return value, so a failed downsize attempt won’t be detected/handled and the code may proceed with an unchanged/oversized tempfile. However, this behavior appears intentional per the added comment (“allow users to upload large images…reduced”), so calling it a definite ‘bug’/data loss is arguable rather than unequivocally incorrect behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public OptimizedImage.resize/downsize signatures changed from (from, to, width, height, opts) to (from, to, dimensions, opts), so all existing in-tree callers still passing width and height as separate args now pass height into the opts slot. Callers like create_optimized_image invoke downsize(from, to, w, h, opts): w becomes the dimensions string, h lands in opts, and opts[:allow_animation] raises NoMethodError on an Integer (or silently skips the animated branch), so every optimized-image generation path that calls the old 4-arg form breaks at runtime after this diff deploys.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` is defined twice after the diff: first with the old `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` signature, then again later as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition overrides the earlier one, so the effective public signature becomes `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Any existing callers still using the old 4-arg/5-arg form (`downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)`) would now raise `ArgumentError` for wrong number of arguments at runtime. The diff does not show any updates to other callers, so this is a real breaking change introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes 10MB and the 413 handler hardcodes the same value, discarding the SiteSettings-driven limits (max_image_size_kb and max_<type>_size_kb) that admins configure. Admins who set max_*_size_kb below 10MB can no longer enforce it client-side — oversized files are uploaded, then either silently downsized server-side or rejected with a misleading 'max_size_kb: 10240' message that contradicts the configured setting; config is silently ignored with no migration of the setting value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the client-side max size limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` and similarly hardcodes `10 * 1024` for the 413 handler, so admin-configured `max_<type>_size_kb` / `max_image_size_kb` are no longer reflected client-side and the error message will report 10240KB regardless of configured limits. The server-side also changes URL download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`, further ignoring the setting for that path. This is a verifiable behavior regression from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit and writes its output to /dev/null), so a failed ImageMagick conversion leaves the original oversized tempfile in place and the upload proceeds. When ImageMagick is missing, fails on a corrupt/animated image, or repeatedly cannot shrink below the limit, the controller silently uploads a file larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and returns success — the API reports success while dropping the size-enforcement work the feature exists to provide.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks whether it succeeded (and never verifies at the end that `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`). In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` on non-zero exit status (and otherwise returns nil), so a failed ImageMagick conversion leaves the oversized tempfile unchanged; the loop just decrements `attempt` and then `Upload.create_for(...)` is invoked regardless. The diff shows no handling for failure/bailout, so the intended “auto reduce” enforcement can silently not happen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes 10*1024 KB instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the alert can display a limit that is not the site's actual configured limit. On a site with max_image_size_kb set below 10MB, users uploading a 9MB image see no client-side error (correct, it will be downsized), but on any file type routed through this shared validator the user is told the limit is 10240 KB while the server enforces a different configured value — the error content misdirects debugging and misrepresents the enforced limit.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, both the generic size check and the 413 handler replace `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB. This makes the client-side limit and the error message always report 10MB regardless of the site’s configured per-type limits, while the server-side logic in `uploads_controller.rb` still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (and other types’ enforcement is not shown as changed). That mismatch can mislead users/debugging and can allow the client to pass a file size the server may reject under a lower configured limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10 MB in the user-facing message even though the server that returned 413 enforced the web server's own configured body limit, which may be smaller or larger. A user whose 20MB upload is rejected by nginx with 413 is told the max size is 10240 KB; if the reverse proxy limit is 5MB the message is wrong, and if the admin set a larger limit the message understates what is allowed — misleading error content on a user-facing path.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 handler was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). That makes the user-facing error message always report 10240 KB regardless of the actual upload limit that triggered the 413 (which could be controlled by proxy/web server or different site settings), so the message can be incorrect/misleading as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loop attempts 5 downsizes with no break on conversion failure and no logging, so 5 identical failing ImageMagick invocations run per oversized upload with no observability of why the file was still oversized. On a site with a broken ImageMagick install, every large-image upload pays 5 wasted subprocess spawns (a per-request amplification on the upload path) and operators get no signal that downsizing never worked — the feature is silently inert until a user complains.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop runs up to 5 times purely based on `tempfile.size` (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...`). It calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores any success/failure signal. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on nonzero exit status, so a failing ImageMagick invocation won’t change the file size and the loop will retry 5 times, spawning 5 identical failing subprocesses. There is also no logging/exception handling in this loop, so failures are silent and the feature can be inert with wasted work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public OptimizedImage.downsize signature changes from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions-string) while keeping the same method name, so any existing caller still passing two numeric arguments silently produces the malformed geometry string "80x50%"-style input instead of failing loudly at a renamed method. In-tree or plugin callers of downsize that were not updated pass (w, h) and get a single "WxH"-interpreted string built from "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" only if they happen to pass two args — a caller passing two numbers now hits ArgumentError on the 3-arg arity, but a caller adapted to pass one string in the old percent format is indistinguishable from a caller passing a broken dimension; a rename to downsize_by_dimensions would have made stale callers fail loudly instead of producing corrupt convert instructions.

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb the PR ends up defining `self.downsize` twice: first with the old `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`-style body (converted to a geometry string), then later redefining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, which overrides the earlier definition in Ruby. That means the effective public signature has changed to a “dimensions string” form, and any existing callers (especially plugins/out-of-tree) still passing `(w, h, opts)` could now misbind arguments (e.g., a 4-arg call `(from,to,w,h)` would treat `h` as `opts`) or otherwise break. The diff itself doesn’t show any remaining in-tree callers using the old signature, so the breakage isn’t directly verifiable here, but the API change risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsizing feature is gated directly on the raw SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb value with no dedicated setting, so admins who want to keep a strict upload limit have no way to disable auto-downsizing, and the client hardcode means the effective behavior cannot be turned off without a code deploy. An admin whose compliance policy requires rejecting oversized files outright gets them silently shrunk and accepted instead; there is no feature flag or setting to restore the previous reject behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds unconditional server-side auto-downsizing for images when `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0` (uploads_controller.rb: new `while ... tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize`). There is no separate setting/flag to preserve prior behavior of rejecting oversized images while still enforcing an upload limit. Additionally, the client-side size limit is hardcoded to 10MB in utilities.js (`maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) rather than using `Discourse.SiteSettings`, removing admin configurability on the client. This is a configurability/behavior-change concern rather than a strictly verifiable correctness defect in the diff itself.
